audit.whatIsWrong: This side records 54.84% over 31 games; Nasus's own page records 52.56% over 567 games for the same matchup. Those cannot both be right — the mirror implies 47.44% here.
audit.why: MC_WR_TABLES.galio.nasus = 54.84 with MC_REAL_GAMES 31; MC_WR_TABLES.nasus.galio = 52.56 with 567 games. Sample sizes differ by 18x.
audit.corrected: No edit made — win rate is not a writable path and I will not invent a number. Raised in questionsForUser.

audit.why: Galio's chart reads Galio / Galio / Galio / Galio / Skill / Nasus / Nasus and Nasus's page carries the identical array, so the two directions already agree. Difficulty 6/10 with Nasus carry threat 10/10 matches a lane Galio owns early and loses to stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings call Hero's Entrance global and one gives it a taunt: 'your R taunt-knockup swings it', 'your global presence dwarfs', 'Use R to roam... your global presence', 'Hero's Entrance gives you a global all-in'.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 at range 4000/4750/5500, must be cast onto an ALLY, and knocks up rather than taunts. The mirror audit at audits/top/nasus__galio.json already corrected the same error in five strings from Nasus's side, so leaving it here would have put the two pages in direct conflict.
audit.corrected: Restated as landing on an ally up to 4000 units away for a knockup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is named nine times but never connected to the Shield of Durand charge, which is the interaction that decides the lane.
audit.why: Riot has Galio 'charges a defensive stance, MOVING SLOWLY' with the taunt only on release, and Wither reaches 700 and decelerates move and attack speed. A Galio who begins the charge outside his own 275 taunt radius gets Withered mid-crawl and never arrives. The mirror states the same interaction from Nasus's side ('Wither him mid-charge and he never closes'), so both pages now agree.
audit.corrected: Punch in first, then charge and release. Written into early, whys[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], loading and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the Sands is described only as 'R lifesteal' and 'his R heals through everything'.
audit.why: Riot: 'he gains increased Health, Attack Range, damages nearby enemies, has a reduced cooldown on Siphoning Strike, and gains bonus Armor and MAGIC RESISTANCE.' The magic resist is the part that matters to an AP Galio — his ultimate directly blunts your damage for its duration, on a 120-second cooldown at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Disengage through Fury of the Sands rather than fighting into it. Written into late, whys[6] and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] reads 'his W amps only magic damage, which is irrelevant against his physical Q'.
audit.why: Nasus's W is Wither, which amplifies nothing. The magic amplification belongs to Galio's own Shield of Durand, so the pronoun makes the sentence assign a Galio mechanic to Nasus.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as YOUR W, with Siphoning Strike named as the physical damage it fails to amplify against.

edits.before: This is your window. He cannot fight back through 4-5 — he just farms — so keep poking with the Q tornado and denying stacks while you control the wave. At 6, Hero's Entrance is your real weapon: even if he hugs tower and refuses to trade, you flag another lane or a fight and drop in with the taunt-knockup, so a passive Nasus literally hands you the map. Keep punishing his step-ups with Q-into-W-taunt, but once his Q is maxed and ramping, do not sit in melee range trading blow-for-blow — his empowered last-hit Q starts hitting harder than your kit, and your W's magic damage reduction is wasted on his physical Q.
edits.after: This is your window. He cannot fight back through 4-5 — he just farms — so keep poking with the Q tornado and denying stacks while you control the wave. Your 825 tornado sits outside his entire kit: Siphoning Strike is 255, Spirit Fire 650, Wither 700. At 6, Hero's Entrance is your real weapon: even if he hugs tower and refuses to trade, you land on an ally 4000 units away and knock up a fight he cannot reach, so a passive Nasus hands you the map. Keep punishing step-ups with Q-into-W-taunt, but once his Q is maxed do not sit in melee trading — his empowered swing outpaces your kit and your reduction is wasted on physical damage.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and no engage, and he is just starting to stack Q, so nobody wins the opener. Your lane begins at 2-3: fire Q's converging windblasts into the lingering tornado to chunk him whenever he steps up for a Q last-hit, since the center column hits hardest and his only answer is to eat it or give up the stack. Once you have W and E, charge Shield of Durand and release the taunt as he walks up, then Justice Punch through him for the knockup — he has no dash and no escape, so the trade is free. Note his W is Wither, not a damage tool early; he has nothing to punish your poke with until his Q ramps.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and no engage, and he is just starting to stack Q, so nobody wins the opener. Your lane begins at 2-3: fire Q's converging windblasts into the lingering tornado to chunk him whenever he steps up for a Q last-hit, since the center column hits hardest and his only answer is to eat it or give up the stack. Once you have W and E the order matters: Shield of Durand makes you crawl while it charges and Wither reaches 700, so never start the charge from outside your own 275 taunt radius — punch in first, then charge and release. His W is Wither, not a damage tool; he has nothing to punish your poke with until his Q ramps.

edits.before: Your full Q-W-E combo lands — channel Shield of Durand, release the taunt as he steps up, then Justice Punch the knockup on a champion with no dash to escape.
edits.after: Your full combo lands, but order it: Justice Punch in first, then charge Shield of Durand — starting the crawl at range hands him a free 700-range Wither.

edits.before: Respect the scaling completely. Once he has 2+ items and a few hundred Q stacks, Wither slows your movement and attack speed to nothing while his Q deletes you and his R heals through everything — your tank-AP damage plateaus while his keeps climbing. Never duel him in a sidelane after this point; your job is to be the teamfight button. Group, save R for the fight, and let your taunt-knockup peel a carry or catch his backline instead of trying to stat-check a champion built to out-stat you.
edits.after: Respect the scaling completely. Once he has 2+ items and a few hundred Q stacks, Wither slows your movement and attack speed to nothing while his Q deletes you. Fury of the Sands is worse than it looks: it grants him bonus magic resist on top of the health, so your AP damage drops exactly when you need it, and it runs 120 seconds at rank 1 — disengage and come back after. Never duel him in a sidelane; group, save R for the fight, and let the taunt-knockup peel a carry instead of stat-checking a champion built to out-stat you.

edits.after: Nasus out-scales hard, and Fury of the Sands hands him bonus magic resist just as your AP peaks — stop dueling and play teamfights.

notes: Mirror-driven. audits/top/nasus__galio.json had already found that Galio's ultimate is called GLOBAL across the Nasus page and corrected five strings; the Galio side carried the same error in four strings plus a fabricated 'R taunt-knockup', so both are now fixed and agree. Reused rather than re-derived: Hero's Entrance 180/160/140 at 4000/4750/5500 onto an ally, Justice Punch 11s to 7s, and the Shield-of-Durand-is-a-charge interaction — stated here from Galio's side as 'punch in before you start the crawl, because Wither reaches 700'. New from this side: Fury of the Sands grants bonus MAGIC RESIST, which the page reduced to 'R lifesteal', and that is the specific reason an AP Galio's damage falls off during his 120-second ultimate. Also fixed a pronoun error in whys[5] that attributed Galio's magic-amplified reduction to Nasus's W. FALSE POSITIVE confirmed: the packet flagged 'Spirit Visage' in wants.foe[1] as a mangled 'Spirit Fire' — it is the item, correctly used, and was left alone.
